tonight.headline: Your 76% is an unset lineup, not a lead. Do not manage the week as if you are ahead.
body: ESPN's live projection has this 119.6 to 70.9 and puts you at 76%. That 70.9 is not a weak roster. KEI returns have four starting slots empty — both wide receiver spots, the defence and the kicker — and Drake London at 15.5, George Pickens at 14.8, the 49ers defence at 7.4 and Evan McPherson at 7.9 are all sitting on their bench.

If they set that lineup any time before Sunday at 11:00 they add roughly 45.6 points and this becomes 119.6 to 116.5. They have already made lineup moves this week — eight of them on Wednesday afternoon — so they are not an absent manager. Treat the game as a coin flip, not a win, and do not leave points on your own bench on the strength of the number.

case.label: What the 76% is actually measuring
case.body: The win probability reads the slots as they stand now. Four empty starting slots score zero, and ESPN prices that as a 48.7-point deficit. Nothing about KEI returns' roster quality produces that gap: they own De'Von Achane, Cam Skattebo, Travis Etienne Jr., Jaxson Dart and Tyler Warren in the slots they have filled, plus Patrick Mahomes at 17.3 on the bench.

case.label: Why it is not safe to assume they forget
case.body: Their activity log shows eight lineup changes on 16 September between 16:58 and 17:00 UTC, including moves for Parker Washington, Kalif Raymond, George Pickens, Travis Etienne Jr., Cam Skattebo, the 49ers defence and Evan McPherson. A manager who made eight moves on Wednesday is a manager who sets a lineup.

case.label: The one place it changes your behaviour
case.body: It does not change your starters — your nine are already the highest-projecting legal nine. It changes whether you treat Sunday as a game you can coast through. You cannot. You are the higher-projecting roster by three points once their lineup is set, not by forty-nine.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: KEI returns leaving those four slots empty through Sunday's 11:00 kickoffs. Drake London, Pickens and McPherson all play at 11:00 or later, so the moment passes at 11:00 Mexico City on Sunday and not before. Nothing you do affects it either way.

doFirst.title: Send Team 13: Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson
doFirst.subtitle: Re-verified on this snapshot rather than carried. Lamar is still slot 20 on their bench, Josh Allen is still their starter and is not being asked for, and Lamar is not on Baltimore's injury report.

case.label: Their surplus, checked against the slot column today
case.body: Team 13 hold Josh Allen at slot 0 and Lamar Jackson at slot 20. In a one-QB league the second one scores nothing every week. Their weakest filled starting slot is RB2: Rachaad White at 164.6 behind Christian McCaffrey at 327.1, with only Blake Corum at 158.0 behind him. The slot column was re-read on this 21:52 snapshot, not taken from yesterday — this brief's own log records a run that once wrote 'the quarterback they give up never plays' about a team's starting quarterback.

case.label: The arithmetic, recomputed from this snapshot
case.body: Their optimal season lineup goes 1969.9 to 2010.5, a gain of 40.6. Yours goes 2071.4 to 2087.4, a gain of 16.0. Your baseline is 4.4 lower than it was yesterday because you dropped Matthew Stafford at 07:12 on Wednesday and he was your optimal quarterback at 286.4 against Trevor Lawrence at 282.0. The trade is worth more to you today than it was yesterday, for a reason you would rather not have.

case.label: Why Tuten is the right man to sell
case.body: Draft Sharks had him at 15 carries for 66 yards in Week 1, with Chris Rodriguez Jr. taking the only goal-line snap and five of the eight short-yardage plays while running two more pass routes on five fewer snaps. A back with no goal line and no passing down is the single worst asset type in full PPR — STRATEGY.md section 2 names it. FTN's Week 2 start/sit column says sit him at Denver. He is your flex fallback behind Matthew Golden and nothing more.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Two of them. First, the arithmetic runs on seasonProj, and Tuten's seasonProj has read exactly 205.2 on three consecutive daily snapshots while his weekly number moved — so the +40.6 you are quoting them may be August's opinion rather than today's. Second, this is the eighth version of an offer to the same manager. If it is declined again by Friday the read on him is wrong and the offer stops rather than being reskinned.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second running back, which kills the +40.6. Or they trade or drop a quarterback, which kills the surplus. Or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report — he was not on Wednesday's, which listed Zay Flowers, Trey Hendrickson, Ronnie Stanley and four others but not him. Or both this and the Golden version are declined by Friday.

whatWentWrong.title: Dropping Stafford cost you 4.4 season points and made Lawrence your only quarterback
whatWentWrong.lead: At 07:12 Wednesday you dropped Matthew Stafford to claim Zach Charbonnet. Stafford was your optimal-lineup quarterback at 286.4 against Lawrence's 282.0, and he is on waivers in this league until 01:00 Saturday.

case.label: The measured cost
case.body: Your optimal season lineup read 2075.8 with Stafford on the roster and reads 2071.4 without him. That is the whole of the difference — 4.4 points — and it is small. It matters because of what it did to your shape, not its size.

case.label: Why it changes today's card
case.body: You now carry one quarterback. Lawrence projects 14.8 this week at Denver, which the FantasyPros Week 2 primer flags as one of the harder quarterback draws on the slate, and there is no second option on your bench. That is precisely why the Lamar card at the top of this brief is ELITE rather than SOLID: it is no longer an upgrade, it is the repair.

case.label: Do not buy him back
case.body: He is on waivers at 90.8% rostered until 01:00 Saturday, and a claim in this league spends the waiver priority you have never spent. See the Do-not-chase row. If you want him back, wait for him to clear to free agency — and by then you should have Lamar instead.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Lawrence clearing 18 points at Denver would say the gap was never real. Team 13 accepting the Lamar offer retires the whole question.

whatWentWrong.title: Zach Charbonnet is a dead bench seat, and the right move is still to leave him there
whatWentWrong.lead: He came in on the same 07:12 transaction, he is OUT with a shoulder described as indefinite, he started the season on PUP, and this league sets slot 21 to zero so there is no IR to park him in.

case.label: What the seat costs
case.body: One of five bench places, at a 0.0 projection, in a week where the wire holds T.J. Hockenson at 64.1% rostered and Jake Ferguson at 82.1% as free agents. That is the real price, not the points.

case.label: Why I am not proposing the drop
case.body: He arrived thirty-nine hours ago. STRATEGY.md section 3 closes a seat that has changed hands inside seven days and says in terms that reversing a move made two days ago is never right — it has happened twice on this roster and gained nothing both times. Dropping him today would also gain nothing this week: he scores zero whether he is rostered or not, and the seat cannot be filled with a starter.

case.label: The upside that justifies the wait
case.body: Seattle's backfield behind Kenneth Walker III is worth a stash if the shoulder is short. I could not find a dated return timeline from Seattle this run either, which is the second consecutive run that search has come back empty.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Tuesday 22 September, when the churn window expires — unless Seattle publish a timeline longer than three weeks before then, or he is still OUT on the Week 4 report, either of which makes it a drop the same day. If he practises or is activated, the stash worked and this closes right.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +40.6 across the season against your +16.0 — two and a half times yours, and saying so in the message is what gets it read instead of ignored.

case.label: The shape
case.body: One for one, and the best player in the deal comes to you. STRATEGY.md section 7 says to trade into the other side's urgency and names this exact structure: a team carrying two elite quarterbacks in a one-QB league is paying for nothing every week. Team 13 are 0-1 with Josh Allen starting and Lamar Jackson idle.

case.label: What each side is actually fixing
case.body: They convert a quarterback who cannot play into a starting running back — Tuten's 205.2 replaces Rachaad White's 164.6 at RB2, worth 40.6. You convert a flex body into the quarterback position outright: Lamar's 312.9 replaces Lawrence's 282.0, and Matthew Golden's 190.3 slides into the flex Tuten vacates, worth 16.0.

case.label: The risk, stated in the words the runbook asks for
case.body: This offer only clears the bar on a season horizon. On Sunday alone Lamar projects 20.6 against Lawrence's 14.8, a gain of 5.8, and Golden replacing Tuten in the flex gives most of that back. If you are managing week to week this is a small trade. On sixteen weeks it is the difference between a QB2 and the consensus QB2 overall.

case.label: The number I do not trust
case.body: Both gains are priced on seasonProj, and Tuten's seasonProj has been 205.2 on three consecutive daily snapshots while his weekly projection moved. If those totals are preseason artifacts, the +40.6 is August's view of Tuten and not this week's, and the proposal is less generous than it reads. It still favours them on any reading, which is why the odds are LIKELY.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second running back; or trade or drop a quarterback; or Lamar appears on a Baltimore injury report — he was not on the Wednesday report. If this and the Golden version are both declined by Friday, stop offering.

trades.sources: ESPN league data · Russell Street Report · Draft Sharks
trades.copyText: Hey — would you do Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson? You're carrying Lamar behind Josh Allen in a one-QB league, so he scores you nothing every week, and your RB2 is Rachaad White at 164 for the season. Tuten's at 205 and he'd start for you immediately — by my math that's about +41 to your season total against +16 to mine. I know that's lopsided in your favour; I need a quarterback more than I need a fourth back. Let me know.

worthALook.name: T.J. Hockenson
worthALook.lead: Minnesota's second target behind Justin Jefferson — ahead of every receiver on the roster — and free in a league whose flex takes a tight end.

case.label: The role
case.body: FantasyLife have Hockenson as Minnesota's number two target behind Jefferson at 81% route share and 16% target share, which puts him ahead of Jordan Addison in the order. In this league that matters twice: the flex is slot 23 and takes a tight end, so a second startable one is a real asset rather than the dead weight it is in Chem.

case.label: Why the quarterback change helps rather than hurts
case.body: Kyler Murray is in concussion protocol and Carson Wentz likely starts at Chicago. Wentz entered in Week 1 and the Minnesota passing game did not degrade — Jefferson went 8 of 9 for 92 and two scores against Green Bay. A backup who knows the plan tends to throw more to the safety valves, not fewer. Ownership moved +1.45 today, the largest rise of any tight end on this wire.

case.label: Why he is not a card
case.body: Your five bench seats are Tuten, Lloyd, Mayer, Charbonnet and Vele. Tuten is the trade chip and cannot be dropped while the offer is live. Charbonnet's seat is closed by the churn rule until 22 September. Vele arrived at 15:04 today. Lloyd and Mayer are the only genuinely open seats and both have live reasons to stay — Mayer starts for Las Vegas this week with Bowers absent from Thursday practice. There is no clean drop, and STRATEGY.md is explicit that a move has to be worth the churn.

case.label: When to act
case.body: The moment the Lamar trade is accepted or formally dead, which frees Tuten's seat either way. Or if Colston Loveland draws under four targets against Minnesota on Sunday, which breaks the tight end thesis and turns a second startable TE from a luxury into a need. He is a free agent, so no priority is involved whenever you do it.

worthALook.name: Pat Freiermuth
worthALook.lead: The only MONEY-band player at tight end on this wire, carried forward from yesterday and unchanged by anything today.

case.label: The signal
case.body: 20.7% rostered and up 1.50 on the day, which is the fourth-largest rise on the IPADE board and the only tight end flagged MONEY — low ownership rising fast. STRATEGY.md section 4 ranks ownership velocity fourth and calls it a lagging confirmation of a role change, which is exactly how to treat it.

case.label: What I could not confirm
case.body: I did not find a Pittsburgh beat report this run naming a role change behind the ownership move, and I am not going to invent one. Without it this is a number moving, not a thing happening. That is the difference between this row and the Hockenson row above it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A Pittsburgh report giving him a route or red-zone share increase, or a Week 2 line above six targets at New England. Either turns the velocity into a role and he becomes the better version of the Hockenson add, because he would be cheaper to hold.

doNotChase.name: Jason Myers
doNotChase.lead: Clears waivers at 01:00 Friday Mexico City, nine hours from now, and claiming him would spend the only waiver priority you have all season on a kicker.

case.label: The clock, converted
case.body: 07:00 UTC on 18 September is 01:00 Friday in Mexico City. This 16:00 brief is the last one before it. He is 96.9% rostered nationally and K5 on the board, so the temptation is real and the answer is still no.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: Priority. IPADE's waiver order never resets — one claim drops you from 3rd of 10 to last for the whole season. STRATEGY.md section 6 spends it only on a player who starts immediately or wins a league, and names streamers and bye-week patches as the things it is never for. Myers projects 9.4 against Cam Little's 8.1. You would spend a season-long asset for 1.3 points in a week.

case.label: And the incumbent is fine
case.body: PFN have Little K3 this week, two places above Myers. The honest caveat is unchanged from yesterday: Little kicks at Denver with Jacksonville implied for only 21.5, so rank and environment disagree. I take the rank, because a kicker's season position is leg and volume and one week of matchup moves it little.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing involving waivers. If Myers clears unclaimed and becomes a free agent, the comparison reopens at zero cost and the answer may well be different — that is exactly what happened with Jake Ferguson this week.

doNotChase.name: Matthew Stafford
doNotChase.lead: You cut him thirty-nine hours ago, he is on waivers at 90.8% rostered until 01:00 Saturday, and buying him back at that price would be the worst transaction of your season.

case.label: Why it is tempting
case.body: He was your optimal-lineup quarterback at 286.4 season and he projects 17.4 this week against Lawrence's 14.8. You now carry one quarterback, into the week Lawrence draws Denver. Every part of that pulls toward reclaiming him.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: He is WAIVERS, not FREEAGENT, until 07:00 UTC Saturday. Claiming him spends the season's waiver priority — 3rd of 10, never spent, never resets — to undo a move you made yourself on Wednesday. That is a churn paid for with a season-long asset, and STRATEGY.md section 6 rules it out on both counts independently.

case.label: The better version of the same fix
case.body: The Lamar card at the top of this brief. It costs Bhayshul Tuten, who is your fourth running back and whom FTN tell you to bench this week, and it delivers a better quarterback than Stafford at 312.9 against 286.4. If it lands, this row never needs writing again.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Stafford clearing to free agency at 01:00 Saturday with the Lamar deal already declined. At zero cost and with one quarterback on the roster, he becomes a reasonable free-agent add — and the drop would be Charbonnet, whose churn window expires the following Tuesday.

doNotChase.name: Jake Ferguson
doNotChase.lead: The loudest ownership anomaly in this league is now a free agent, so the cost argument has gone — and the answer is still no, on role.

case.label: What changed and what did not
case.body: He cleared waivers unclaimed, which is exactly what yesterday's thesis said would reopen the question. Acquiring him now costs no priority at all, so STRATEGY.md section 6 no longer applies. Nine managers passed on him at zero cost and they were right.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: 18.6 points per game without CeeDee Lamb, 8.9 with him. Lamb projects 18.8 this week and is ACTIVE; George Pickens projects 14.8 and is ACTIVE. Ferguson is PFN's TE16 and the third read in his own offence, with Ryan Flournoy eating in from below. Ownership moved -0.51 today: a market walking away, not one that has not noticed.

case.label: And he loses the seat to a better TE
case.body: If you are adding a tight end into this league's TE-eligible flex, T.J. Hockenson is the second target in his offence rather than the third, and he is free on the same wire. Ferguson is the more famous name and the worse add.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens appearing on a Dallas injury report — Ferguson then becomes the best free agent in this league and the seat is his the same hour.

settled.title: Start Matthew Golden in the RB/WR/TE flex over Tuten (15 September)

settled.result: Holding, and firmer today than yesterday. Brock Bowers was absent from Thursday's practice after not practising Wednesday. Mayer started for Las Vegas in Week 1 without him and went 6 catches on 7 targets, and the Chargers have allowed the 5th-most fantasy points per target to tight ends.

settled.title: Hold Cam Little at kicker (16 September)
settled.result: Holding, fifth consecutive run. PFN have Little K3. The best available here is Jason Myers at K5 and he is on waivers, which makes him a non-option; then Will Reichard, Chase McLaughlin and Cairo Santos, none of whom beat him by a point.

settled.title: Add the Ravens defence as a free agent, drop the Jaguars (16 September)
settled.result: Holding. PFN have Baltimore 9th of 32 this week against a New Orleans offence ranked 26th; Jacksonville are 10th but on waivers here. No priority was spent because Baltimore was a free agent — that distinction is the whole reason this was a good move.

settled.title: Decline Jake Ferguson even once he became free (17 September)
settled.result: Holding, on role rather than cost. 8.9 points per game with CeeDee Lamb active, and Lamb is active. Re-checked today with nothing changed.

settled.title: Do not offer Garrett Wilson for Josh Allen (16 September)
settled.result: Holding. The pair search surfaces it again today at +21.3 me and +21.8 them, the largest mutual-gain pair in the league, and it is still not to be sent. Allen is Team 13's starting quarterback and the consensus QB1 overall; STRATEGY.md section 7 makes any top-five player untouchable regardless of the math and names this exact failure mode.

settled.title: Add Devaughn Vele, drop Kayshon Boutte (16 September)
settled.result: Executed at 15:04 today as a free agent, no priority spent. Chris Olave was not on Baltimore week's injury report, which leaves Vele the clear number two on a 90.7% snap share rather than the beneficiary of an absence. This one is done and moves off the card list.

settled.title: Claim Zach Charbonnet, drop Matthew Stafford (owner move, 07:12 Wednesday)
settled.result: A dead bench seat and 4.4 season points, and it is not reversible this week. Charbonnet is OUT with an indefinite shoulder, this league has no IR slot, and Stafford is now on waivers at 90.8% rostered. The churn rule says leave both alone until 22 September.

settled.title: Start Stafford over Lawrence (16 September), withdrawn 17 September
settled.result: Still a miss and now permanently settled by the drop. A card marked ELITE that flipped inside nine hours should never have been ELITE, and the player it concerned is no longer on the roster.

settled.title: Hold Colston Loveland at tight end with confidence lowered (16 September)
settled.result: Unresolved and I am flagging it as a miss in advance rather than after. Two targets and no catches in a 59-point game is a targeting problem on the box score. Bleacher Nation's tape review argues the opposite — 27 pass plays as a designed decoy, Carolina's coordinator refusing to let a linebacker cover him, spacing created for Kmet. I lean to the tape, but the falsification condition fires on Sunday if he is under four targets again, and two weeks of that beats any tape read.

cannotSee.label: Whether Team 13 have read the offer, or any of the previous seven
cannotSee.body: There is no PROPOSE button — this league's trade write is unmapped, so the card gives you the message and you send it in ESPN. I cannot see whether it was opened, declined or never noticed. The thesis says that if this and the Golden version are both declined by Friday the read on that manager is wrong and the offer stops. Friday is tomorrow.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are frozen, which undercuts the arithmetic in the trade card
cannotSee.body: Bhayshul Tuten's seasonProj has read exactly 205.2 on the 15, 16 and 17 September snapshots while his weekly projection moved from 9.4 to 10.1. The trade math produces the identical +40.6 on all three. The weekly number is live; the season number looks like a preseason artifact. Every figure in the trade card and the pair search is priced on it, so treat +40.6 and +16.0 as directionally right and numerically soft.

cannotSee.label: Eleven of your fourteen matchup tiles are not researched
cannotSee.body: I graded three this run: Denver against quarterbacks for Lawrence, Baltimore for the defence, and the Chargers against tight ends for Mayer. Kansas City, Tennessee, Indianapolis, Green Bay, Minnesota, the Jets, Arizona and Denver-against-running-backs are dashed because I did not look them up, not because they are average. Lawrence's SHAKY comes from a primer note that Denver are tough on quarterbacks rather than from a numbered rank, which is the softest of the three.

cannotSee.label: Who is throwing to Garrett Wilson, corroborated but not confirmed
cannotSee.body: He starts in both of your leagues, so this is the one worth being precise about. I could not retrieve a beat report naming the Jets' Week 2 starter — two searches and the ESPN depth chart, which came back blank. Two independent routes give the same answer: Geno Smith at 14.0 projected here is the only quarterback New York have anywhere in this data set, and this morning's run reached the same name from its own research. The other quarterbacks in this brief — Jones for Taylor, Hurts for Barkley, Mahomes for Rice, Williams for Loveland, Love for Golden and Lloyd, Cousins for Mayer, Lock for Charbonnet, Shough for Vele — are carried from that run rather than re-verified this afternoon.

cannotSee.label: Brock Bowers's Friday designation, which decides whether Mayer has value next week
cannotSee.body: Absent from practice Wednesday and Thursday, which is why Mayer's tile is green. Schefter had Las Vegas believing he might miss only one game; Dr Deepak Chona read the same meniscus trim as a two-week ramp with week 3 more likely. If Bowers returns in Week 3, Mayer's seat becomes the open one and Hockenson is the add.

cannotSee.label: Zach Charbonnet still has no return date
cannotSee.body: Second consecutive run in which no dated Seattle timeline could be found. Out indefinitely with a shoulder after starting the season on PUP is everything that has been published. The seat is dead for Week 2 either way, so the cost of not knowing is deferred to 22 September rather than paid now.

cannotSee.label: Rival pending claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN only ever returns your own. T.J. Hockenson at 64.1% and Jake Ferguson at 82.1% are free agents right now and either can be taken before you next open this. Jason Myers and Matthew Stafford clear waivers at 01:00 Friday and 01:00 Saturday and I cannot see who has claims in on them.

cannotSee.body: It is a photograph of 21:52 UTC on Thursday. No IPADE starter plays before Sunday at 11:00 Mexico City, so every designation in it has two more practice reports to go. Re-check Loveland, Vele and the Jets quarterback before then.
